classification: Realtime delivery-path corrections: OKX native bars reach the canonical stream, the durable spool stops failing writes closed inside its own retention policy, and the projector stops paying a thread hop per record.

delta.defect: Three independent defects. (1) Every closed OKX candle was quarantined StaleGeneration and no OKX bar ever reached md.canonical.v2: the ingestor runs one socket per feed class with its own connection generation counter, and the ordering fence compared counters from different lanes as bare integers before it looked at the session. (2) The durable spool failed every canonical write closed for two hours at a 3 GiB physical bound while still inside its own row policy, because PASSIVE checkpoints recycle a WAL without shrinking the file. (3) The 3.8M event backlog that followed could not drain: consumption had converged on production at 759 events/s with projectors at 0.49 of a 2.00 CPU ceiling and the volume able to absorb 40,280 rows/s.

slices.R1.25.1: connection generations are compared within one provider lane; an unparsable session id keeps the original comparison
slices.R1.25.2: the projector fetches a bounded batch in one broker call; brokers without it keep the original fill loop
slices.R1.25.3: the spool reclaims a WAL that outgrew its declared journal_size_limit, and reclaims again before the physical bound refuses a write
slices.R1.25.4: the physical bound is sized from the rows retention permits
slices.R1.25.5: the canonical sink retries a dead pooled connection once before failing over
slices.R1.25.6: Compose records the broker memory bound raised live after kernel memcg kills at 768m
slices.R1.25.7: the drift verifier seeks the spool by key instead of scanning it, and watches the physical bound

okx_bar_repair.proof_the_fence_was_cross_lane: the bar lane reconnected on its own at 11:29Z from generation 22 to 23 and the brand-new session was quarantined identically

after.method: publish time minus bar close time on md.canonical.v2, final bars only

spool_bound_repair.derivation: 183 physical partitions x a 10,064-record window = 1,841,712 rows; the live cache held 1,301,097 rows in 1,114 MB of payload inside a 2,312 MB file, so the policy needs roughly 3.3 GB on disk before the WAL

projector_throughput.note: the thread hop per record was real but not dominant; the remaining ceiling is the projector's single event-loop thread, recorded as an open measurement rather than a guess

venue_constraints_retested.consequence: Binance MARK_INDEX_PRICE and any native Binance BAR lane cannot be repaired from the WebSocket path; the bar edge's six-second settlement is evidence, not caution

backlog_recovery.replay_is_mostly_discarded: the spool keeps 10,064 records per partition, which is 1.7-2.8 minutes for a busy feed and seven days for BAR 1m: 21 minutes of replay moved the row count by 236, from 1,301,097 to 1,301,333

drift_after_rollout.note: thirteen roles recreated in this rollout introduced no new drift
drift_after_rollout.failing: chain stable_redis - the container records a compose file from a deleted worktree

log_rotation.excluded: stable_redis, deliberately: recreating it destroys the projection cache identity and needs the rebuild runbook, which is not run while a backlog is draining

broker_stability.root_cause: Kafka CLI JVMs exec'd into broker cgroups added ~280 MB each; probes now run in a throwaway container on the stack network

out_of_scope: Binance MARK_INDEX_PRICE: venue does not deliver the WebSocket stream on this host; needs the reference/REST pair path, a catalog migration
native Binance BAR lane: same venue condition, so provider REST remains the outer edge
DNSE VN v2: paused by the owner; openapi.dnse.com.vn:443 unreachable while other DNSE hosts answer
known_open: stable_redis records a compose chain from a deleted worktree and cannot be recreated from its own chain; repair needs a redis recreate plus the projection cache rebuild runbook
with six partitions, three replicas and range assignment, a drained replica cannot take work from a loaded one
